requirements.requirement: Create an opsbot account on node1 (and correspondingly on node2, since it is the SSH target)
requirements.summary: useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsbot succeeded on both node1 and node2, confirmed by id opsbot showing uid=1001(opsbot) on each node.

requirements.requirement: Give opsbot on node1 SSH key-based access to run commands as opsbot on node2
requirements.summary: An ed25519 keypair was generated for opsbot on node1, the public key was installed into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and a BatchMode (no-password) SSH session from node1's opsbot to node2's opsbot succeeded and ran whoami/hostname, returning opsbot/node2. This was re-verified after both nodes were restarted.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems (i.e., disable password authentication)
requirements.summary: sshd -T -C user=opsbot on both node1 and node2 shows pubkeyauthentication yes, passwordauthentication no, kbdinteractiveauthentication no, meaning no password fallback is possible for opsbot specifically. Additionally passwd -S confirms the opsbot account is locked (L, no usable password) on both nodes, reinforcing that only key-based login is possible.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all three material outcomes of the task: an opsbot account exists on both node1 and node2, opsbot on node1 has passwordless, key-based SSH access to run commands as opsbot on node2 (verified both before and after node restarts), and sshd configuration plus account locking confirm key-based authentication is required for opsbot on both systems. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed completely and correctly for both nodes: pre-restart boot identity and healthy baseline were captured, the restart was acknowledged and the node observed unreachable, a new boot identity was captured post-restart, and recovered sshd/opsbot state plus working cross-node key-based SSH were re-verified afterward. The fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate the executor's own restart evidence for both nodes.
limitations: The node2 pre-restart baseline command (cmd-4afb8c1cf02e454f) could not read /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys directly due to permission denial when run outside a sudo -u opsbot wrapper, so the pre-restart authorized_keys content on node2 is inferred rather than directly read; the post-restart check (cmd-9243301e2eb94501) does confirm the file exists with 1 line via sudo -u opsbot.

No independent test of an actual password-authentication rejection (e.g., an attempted password login for opsbot that is refused) was captured; the conclusion that key-based auth is required rests on sshd -T configuration output and account-lock status rather than an observed login attempt.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task or the mandatory restart protocol: useradd+passwd -l on both nodes (task requirement), ed25519 keygen and authorized_keys install (task requirement), ssh-keyscan appending node2's host key to opsbot's known_hosts on node1 (necessary prerequisite for key-based SSH), and the two shutdown -r now reboots (restart protocol, not the public task). One command (cmd-7dd72982557245c3) attempted ssh with an unsupported StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new flag on this older OpenSSH client and failed outright (unsupported option / host key verification failed) without adding any known_hosts entry or other residue; it was immediately superseded by the working ssh-keyscan approach in cmd-f110ad8f408a42a0, so it is a harmless, non-mutating diagnostic misstep rather than an unnecessary mutation. No abandoned files, conflicting services, unsafe exposure, or package-state damage is visible in the before/after-executor diffs, which show only boot-id changes and boot-scoped systemd-private tmp directories expected from the two reboots.
